title: Systemic Light Chain Amyloidosis (AL)
subtitle: Mayo Cardiac Staging, Daratumumab-CyBorD, and Autologous HCT Pathways
provenanceNote: Clinical algorithms extracted from NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 for Systemic Light Chain Amyloidosis.
sourceNote: NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 - Systemic Light Chain Amyloidosis (AMYL-1 to AMYL-4, AMYL-A to AMYL-D)

footnotes.fn_dara_cybord: Daratumumab + CyBorD (ANDROMEDA regimen) is the category 1 standard of care for newly diagnosed AL amyloidosis.
footnotes.fn_cardiac: Cardiac staging by Mayo 2004/2012 criteria governs transplant eligibility and systemic therapy dosing.

nodes.name: Clinical Suspicion
nodes.title: Systemic Light Chain (AL) Amyloidosis: Clinical Presentation
nodes.description: Multisystem disorder caused by tissue deposition of misfolded monoclonal immunoglobulin light chain amyloid fibrils.
bullets: Cardinal clinical presentations: unexplained nephrotic-range proteinuria or renal failure, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and thickened ventricular walls, hepatomegaly without imaging explanation, non-diabetic peripheral/autonomic neuropathy, macroglossia, or spontaneous periorbital ecchymoses ('raccoon eyes').
Urgent evaluation required: Early diagnosis is vital because delayed identification results in irreversible end-organ damage (particularly cardiac failure).

options.label: Previously Treated / Relapsed or Refractory Disease

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: AL Amyloidosis: Mandatory Laboratory, Tissue Biopsy, and Staging Checklist
nodes.description: Establish presence of monoclonal light chain, confirm amyloid fibrils by Congo Red tissue staining/mass spectrometry, and assess organ involvement.
bullets: Serum and Urine Monoclonal Protein Studies: Serum free light chain (sFLC) assay with kappa/lambda ratio and dFLC (difference between involved and uninvolved FLC); serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation (SIFE); 24-hour urine for total protein, electrophoresis (UPEP), and immunofixation (UIFE).

Tissue Biopsy & Definitive Typing: Abdominal subcutaneous fat pad aspirate and/or involved organ biopsy (kidney, bone marrow, salivary gland, rectum, heart). Congo Red staining demonstrating characteristic apple-green birefringence under polarized light.

Mandatory Mass Spectrometry Typing: Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) on Congo-red positive tissue to definitively identify amyloid protein subunit (distinguish AL from ATTR or AA amyloidosis).
Bone Marrow Examination: Aspirate and core biopsy with plasma cell immunohistochemistry and interphase FISH (specifically checking for t(11;14) translocation, present in ~50% of AL amyloidosis).
Cardiac Staging Biomarkers: High-sensitivity Cardiac Troponin T (hs-cTnT) or Troponin I (cTnI), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) or BNP (baseline mandatory for Mayo staging).

Cardiovascular Imaging: 12-lead ECG (low voltage in limb leads discrepant with echocardiographic ventricular thickening); Transthoracic Echocardiogram with global longitudinal strain (apical sparing pattern); Cardiac MRI (diffuse subendocardial or transmural late gadolinium enhancement).

Renal & Coagulation Assessment: BUN, serum creatinine, eGFR, 24-hour urine protein quantification; PT/INR, PTT, and Factor X activity (Factor X deficiency can cause catastrophic hemorrhage in AL amyloidosis).
Blood Bank Typing Alert: Perform blood typing and indirect Coombs test PRIOR to initiating anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody therapy (Daratumumab).

options.label: Workup completed - Perform Mayo cardiac risk staging

nodes.name: Mayo Cardiac Staging
nodes.title: AL Amyloidosis: Mayo Cardiac Prognostic Staging
nodes.description: Stratification based on cardiac biomarkers (hs-cTnT >=40 pg/mL, NT-proBNP >=1800 ng/L, dFLC >=180 mg/L).
bullets: Mayo 2004 / European Modification Staging System:
• Stage I: NT-proBNP <332 ng/L and cTnT <0.035 mcg/L (good prognosis).
• Stage II: Either NT-proBNP >=332 ng/L or cTnT >=0.035 mcg/L.
• Stage IIIa: Both NT-proBNP >=332 ng/L and cTnT >=0.035 mcg/L, with NT-proBNP <8500 ng/L.
• Stage IIIb: Very high cardiac risk (NT-proBNP >=8500 ng/L); prone to early fatal arrhythmias and cardiogenic shock.
Mayo 2012 Staging: Incorporates dFLC >=180 mg/L as 3rd prognostic factor (Stage I: 0 points, Stage II: 1 point, Stage III: 2 points, Stage IV: 3 points).

options.label: Mayo Stage I–IIIa (Standard to Intermediate Cardiac Risk, NT-proBNP <8500 ng/L)
Mayo Stage IIIb (Advanced High-Risk Cardiac Amyloidosis, NT-proBNP >=8500 ng/L)

nodes.name: Autologous HCT Eligibility
nodes.title: Mayo Stage I–IIIa: Evaluation for Autologous Stem Cell Transplant
nodes.description: Rigorous multidisciplinary evaluation to determine candidacy for high-dose melphalan with autologous HCT.
bullets: HCT Eligibility Criteria:
• Age <=65-70 years, ECOG performance status 0-2.
• NYHA Functional Class I-II (compensated cardiac function).
• Cardiac biomarkers: NT-proBNP <5000 ng/L and Troponin T <0.06 mcg/L.
• Preserved organ function: LVEF >=40-45%, DLCO >=50%, eGFR >=30-50 mL/min.

• Definite Exclusions: Medically refractory ventricular/atrial arrhythmias, recurrent pleural effusions, uncompensated heart failure, refractory orthostatic hypotension, Factor X level <25% with bleeding, or extensive bleeding gastrointestinal involvement.

nodes.name: HCT-Eligible Therapy
nodes.title: HCT-Eligible AL Amyloidosis: Induction & Autologous HCT
nodes.description: Frontline Daratumumab-CyBorD induction followed by consolidative autologous HCT or deferred HCT.
bullets: Preferred Induction (2-4 cycles): Daratumumab + Bortezomib + Cyclophosphamide + Dexamethasone (Dara-CyBorD / ANDROMEDA regimen, rare-amyloidosis-dara-cybord). Rapidly reduces clonal light chain burden.
Response-adapted HCT strategy:
• If complete hematologic response (CR, normal FLC ratio and dFLC <10 mg/L) achieved after induction, autologous HCT may be deferred with stem cell harvest and cryopreservation for future relapse.
• If persistent clonal disease / less than CR: Proceed to Autologous HCT with high-dose Melphalan (140-200 mg/m2 risk-adapted based on age and renal function).
Stem cell mobilization: G-CSF +/- Plerixafor; avoid aggressive fluid overhydration and monitor for volume overload.
Post-HCT Maintenance: Single-agent Daratumumab SC monthly may be continued to complete up to 24 cycles per ANDROMEDA trial protocol.
Supportive care: VZV antiviral prophylaxis (acyclovir/valacyclovir), antibacterial prophylaxis during neutropenia, and type/screen maintenance.

nodes.name: Non-Transplant Primary Tx
nodes.title: HCT-Ineligible (Mayo Stage I–IIIa): Daratumumab-CyBorD Therapy
nodes.description: Category 1 standard of care for non-transplant candidates.
bullets: Category 1 Preferred Standard: Daratumumab + Bortezomib + Cyclophosphamide + Dexamethasone (Dara-CyBorD, rare-amyloidosis-dara-cybord).

• Schedule: Daratumumab 1800 mg SC weekly (cycles 1-2), every 2 weeks (cycles 3-6); Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 SC weekly; Cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m2 PO weekly (max 500 mg); Dexamethasone 20-40 mg PO weekly for 6 cycles.
• Maintenance: Single-agent subcutaneous Daratumumab 1800 mg every 4 weeks for up to 24 total cycles (ANDROMEDA trial showed 53% hematologic CR rate and superior organ-free survival).

Neuropathy dose adjustments: For patients with significant peripheral or autonomic neuropathy, bortezomib should be dose-reduced (1.0 or 0.7 mg/m2) or discontinued; alternative regimens include Daratumumab-dexamethasone or Lenalidomide/dexamethasone.
VZV Prophylaxis: Mandatory acyclovir or valacyclovir throughout proteasome inhibitor and daratumumab therapy.

nodes.name: Stage IIIb Advanced Cardiac
nodes.title: Mayo Stage IIIb: Attenuated Therapy & Advanced Cardiac Support
nodes.description: Dose-modified regimens and specialized cardiac management for severe cardiac amyloidosis.
bullets: Urgent multidisciplinary amyloidosis / advanced heart failure center management.
Dose-Modified Systemic Therapy:
• Dose-modified Dara-CyBorD: Attenuated weekly bortezomib (0.7-1.0 mg/m2 SC) + cyclophosphamide (reduced or omitted) + low-dose dexamethasone (10-20 mg weekly).
• Single-agent subcutaneous Daratumumab (1800 mg SC with pre-medication): High efficacy with minimal myocardial toxicity.
Hemodynamic & Heart Failure Management:
• Judicious loop diuretics (bumetanide, torsemide, furosemide) combined with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (spironolactone).

• CONTRAINDICATED DRUGS: Avoid standard heart failure therapies such as beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and calcium channel blockers (diltiazem, verapamil); these cause profound refractory hypotension and heart block due to fixed stroke volume.
• Midodrine or fludrocortisone for refractory orthostatic hypotension.
• Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) / Pacemaker: Considered for high-grade AV block or sustained ventricular arrhythmias.
• Cardiac transplantation evaluation: In highly selected young patients with isolated end-stage cardiac amyloidosis.

nodes.name: Relapsed/Refractory AL
nodes.title: Relapsed / Refractory AL Amyloidosis: Targeted & Novel Regimens
nodes.description: Therapy tailored to prior drug exposure, t(11;14) genetics, and organ tolerance.
bullets: Venetoclax (+/- Dexamethasone): Highly active in patients with t(11;14) translocation (present in ~50% of AL amyloidosis); produces deep hematologic responses in relapsed disease.
Daratumumab-based Therapy: If daratumumab was not administered frontline, single-agent daratumumab or Dara-combinations are strongly recommended.
Immunomodulatory Drugs (IMiDs):
• Pomalidomide (2-4 mg daily days 1-21 q28d) + Dexamethasone: Well-tolerated in bortezomib/daratumumab-refractory disease.
• Lenalidomide (start at low dose 10-15 mg daily days 1-21 q28d) + Dexamethasone.
Oral Proteasome Inhibitors: Ixazomib + Dexamethasone (+/- Cyclophosphamide) - advantageous in patients with mild peripheral neuropathy.
Second Autologous HCT: High-dose melphalan can be considered in eligible patients who achieved prolonged initial remission (>3-5 years) after primary transplant.
Organ Response Monitoring: Monitor sFLC, NT-proBNP, and 24-hour urine protein monthly during salvage therapy.
